title: Before-and-After Photos Confusing? Keep the Order Consistent
description: For a readable before-and-after collage, put the earlier image first and the later image second, then state the order and dates in your accompanying caption.
direct: For a readable before-and-after collage, put the earlier image first and the later image second, then state the order and dates in your accompanying caption. Consistent framing helps viewers compare the actual subject.
figureAlt: The same chair framed consistently before and after a conceptual restoration.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot, measured result or real export.
cards.choice.heading: Decide what is comparable
cards.choice.body: Choose photos of the same subject and, where possible, the same angle and distance. A changed crop, light or pose can exaggerate a difference. Keep the originals so viewers can inspect context when that matters.
sections.explain.heading: Make the comparison easy on phones
sections.explain.body: A narrow screen can hide small details in a horizontal pair. Choose a taller arrangement when both subjects need more width. Inspect the actual shared copy because messaging and social destinations may resize images. Text in an accompanying caption may be separated from the image when forwarded.
sections.practice.heading: Use a truthful example
sections.practice.body: Space Sheep Studio develops our iPhone collage app. It supports 2 to 30 images, eleven layouts and exports up to 3000 pixels wide, with one free export before Pro is required. This guide does not claim an in-app text-labeling tool. The chair restoration illustration is AI-generated, not a customer result or an App export. Do not change either source photo to manufacture a better outcome.

steps.step-1.text: Select the two photos in Combine Photos: Stitch & Grid and choose a side-by-side or suitable stacked arrangement.
steps.step-2.text: Check the sequence in the preview. Move and zoom each photo so the subject has a comparable size without stretching it.
steps.step-3.text: Export JPEG or PNG and inspect the saved collage. Add the dates and “earlier first, later second” in the message or post that accompanies it.
